issue.title: @ContentChildren memory leak with ngTemplateOutlet

labels.name: area: core
labels.description: Issues related to the framework runtime

issue.body:
<!--

**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")
```
[x] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting
[ ] feature request

```

**Current behavior**
<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->
`@ContentChildren` somehow gets hold of children that are passed in a template and instantiated through `[ngTemplateOutlet]`, and never gets rid of them even if they are destroyed.

**Expected behavior**
<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->
I am not sure what the correct behavior for `@ContentChildren` here is (should it see the children or not?) but either way it should not keep a reference to destroyed children. This creates potentially a large memory leak.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
<!--
If the current behavior is a bug or you can illustrate your feature request better with an example, 
please provide the *STEPS TO REPRODUCE* and if possible a *MINIMAL DEMO* of the problem via
https://plnkr.co or similar (you can use this template as a starting point: http://plnkr.co/edit/tpl:AvJOMERrnz94ekVua0u5).
-->
http://plnkr.co/edit/esib13wg0pTmzVEKhNNM?p=preview
Click on the button a few times, you will see that the QueryList keeps growing. On further inspection, you could see that the children in the list are the ones that were destroyed on each previous toggle.

* **Angular version:** 2.4.9
<!-- Check whether this is still an issue in the most recent Angular version -->

* **Browser:** all
<!-- All browsers where this could be reproduced -->
 
* **Language:** all

body:
Hi,
could you make a version that also destroys the component that contains the declaration place of the `<template>`?
@tbosch I'm not sure what I should do. Should I move the templates to a sub-component?
Yes, fixing `ngTemplateOutlet` is the right place.
Thinking about this a bit more, I think we can fix this in a general way, without needing to change `ngTemplateOutlet`... Working on it...
